findings.title: Stop signal does not prevent one more job from being accepted and executed
findings.evidence: The loop checks the stop flag before blocking on the queue, but after a signal arrives during that blocking get, the returned job is still submitted to the pool even though the documented contract says no new jobs are pulled after stop is requested.
findings.recommendation: After get returns, re-check the stop event before submitting. If stop was requested while blocked in get, either put the job back onto the source if supported or avoid fetching with a design that can be interrupted without consuming another item.

findings.title: Consumed queue items are never acknowledged with task_done
findings.evidence: Jobs are read from a queue via get and submitted, but there is no matching completion acknowledgement anywhere in the worker. With a standard queue.Queue source, any caller using join will block forever because unfinished_tasks is incremented by get/put and never decremented.
findings.recommendation: If source is intended to be queue.Queue-compatible, call task_done exactly once per successful get after the job finishes, typically in a finally block inside _run_job or by wrapping the submitted callable. If task_done is not part of the contract, document and enforce a different source interface.
